_note: expired-pause-resumes-the-term (REQ-TERM-080, row 8.10). When a pause runs out without an answer the term resumes by itself, and the case's handler is told. The `hervat` event that records it carries the notice: `notify` is the handler's user id, `caseTitle` and `endDate` are what the message names. Only that automatic resume writes `notify`, so a handler's own resume tells nobody, and the rule's filter reads an absent field on every other event, which fails closed. termijnGebeurtenis 1.3.0.

notify.title: Notify
notify.description: Nextcloud user id this event is told to. Written by dossiq when a term resumes because its pause ran out, never by hand.

caseTitle.title: Case title
caseTitle.description: The title of the case the event is about, as the notification names it.

endDate.title: New end date
endDate.description: The term's end date after this event.

subject.nl: De termijn van zaak "{{caseTitle}}" loopt weer; nieuwe einddatum {{endDate}}
subject.en: The term of case "{{caseTitle}}" is running again; new end date {{endDate}}

message.nl: De opschorting is verlopen zonder antwoord, dus de termijn is vanzelf hervat. De zaak moet nu uiterlijk {{endDate}} beslist zijn.
message.en: The suspension ran out without an answer, so the term resumed by itself. The case now has to be decided by {{endDate}}.
